text: Maani Truu Education correspondent Updated Sep 23, 2026 – 1.14pm , first published at 12.00pm An Australian tutoring company has told parents to invest in Gemini or ChatGPT rather than pay overpriced human tutors to give their children an academic edge, as students increasingly turn to artificial intelligence for exam preparation and immediate study feedback. Dymocks Tutoring and Talent 100, which has five centres across Sydney, will close at the end of the week after telling customers that technology has rendered its service obsolete.
